Reproduce the affine paper results

Source: vignettes/paper-affine-replication.Rmd
paper-affine-replication.Rmd

The installed paper-replication/affine bundle provides three workflows: recreate manuscript displays from saved evidence, rerun the simulation campaign, and fit the SIPP application. It is a study-specific companion to this paper. For general estimation, start with Getting started.

Locate the installed bundle

Install current production source using the README. The historical v0.1.0 release predates this bundle.

bundle <- system.file("paper-replication/affine", package = "RdistNN")
list.files(bundle)
#>  [1] "configs"           "evidence.zip"      "helpers.R"        
#>  [4] "manifest.json"     "README.md"         "render_evidence.R"
#>  [7] "run_simulations.R" "run_sipp.R"        "source"           
#> [10] "verify.R"

Read its README.md for the full protocol and dependencies. manifest.json pins the paper/source identity, accepted configurations and evidence hashes. No paper checkout or original run cache is needed to render the saved results.

Recreate tables and figures without refitting

Install optional rendering dependencies once:

install.packages(c("digest", "jsonlite", "ggplot2", "patchwork"))

Run the portable launcher with a new output directory:

system2(file.path(R.home("bin"), "Rscript"), c(
  shQuote(file.path(bundle, "render_evidence.R")),
  "--output-dir=paper-displays"
))

It verifies the saved evidence, recreates 21 table fragments and six PDF figures, and compares tables with the accepted references. It performs no simulation or estimation. Output manifests record provenance and comparison results. Historical transformed SIPP estimates remain saved evidence because the supplement reports that distinct target; the current fitting workflow uses raw dollars.

Rendering uses Cairo PDF. CRAN R on macOS may require XQuartz, as explained in the R for macOS notes.

Validate the simulation workflow

A smoke run uses two small preflight draw families. It checks execution and outputs; it does not reproduce the production study or provide manuscript evidence.

install.packages(c("digest", "jsonlite", "future", "future.apply"))
system2(file.path(R.home("bin"), "Rscript"), c(
  shQuote(file.path(bundle, "run_simulations.R")),
  "--mode=smoke", "--output-dir=paper-smoke"
))

The full campaign is substantial and requires Linux, Python 3 and the resource budget in the installed README. Use --mode=production with a new directory; --profiles=... selects profiles and --resume requires an identical runtime freeze. The launcher records the executed package, seed/configuration identities and process receipts. Incomplete campaigns are not production evidence; fresh results require review before manuscript promotion.

Validate or rerun the SIPP application

The application studies raw-dollar net financial assets in 9,915 complete households, with full-fit, own-arm OOB and held-out five-fold nuisance predictions. The installed README defines the accepted specification, profiles, orders, seed and export layout.

install.packages(c("hdm", "grf", "digest", "jsonlite"))
system2(file.path(R.home("bin"), "Rscript"), c(
  shQuote(file.path(bundle, "run_sipp.R")),
  "--mode=smoke", "--output-dir=sipp-smoke"
))

Smoke uses a small sample and validation-labelled outputs. Use --mode=production with a new directory for the full application. Output directories are not silently overwritten.

These practical forests, unbounded outcomes and data-selected profiles/scales are outside the bounded-series primitive theorem. Frozen deletions do not refit nuisance learners. Order sensitivity does not estimate localization bias or select an optimal order; full-fit/OOB agreement does not verify a stability rate.

For package-wide argument and covariance conventions, see Notation and conventions.
